problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-8y-4x-16=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

feedback.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}+54x-32y=53.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ terms and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}+54x-32y & =53 \\ (4{y}^{2}-32y)+(-9{x}^{2}+54x) & =53 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-8y]-9[{x}^{2}-6x] & =53 \\ 4[(y-4)^{2}-16]-9[(x-3)^{2}-9] & =53 \\ 4(y-4)^{2}-64-9(x-3)^{2}+81 & =53 \\ 4(y-4)^{2}-9(x-3)^{2} & =53+64-81 \\ 4(y-4)^{2}-9(x-3)^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{4(y-4)^{2}}{36}-\frac{9(x-3)^{2}}{36} & =\frac{36}{36} \\ \frac{(y-4)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(3,4),\,a=\sqrt{9}=3,\,b=\sqrt{4}=2.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
y-4=\pm \frac{3}{2}(x-3).
$$
